_doc: Headset patient flow (Phase 2). Read by headset/Perimetry.Headset.Logic, part of the config hash. Training levels are device dB (0 = device maximum). Field positions in degrees, OD convention (mirrored for OS).

fixationTarget._colorDoc: HFA central fixation target is yellow; rendered at the luminance below, independent of the stimulus scale.

training._doc: 3-5 practice presentations with feedback (SPEC §8). stimulusShown=false is a blank trial that teaches not to press without a light. Training responses are logged but never enter the exam.

checks._doc: Pre-exam verification (SPEC §8.2). Button: the welcome screen only advances on a press. Sharpness: the patient confirms the fixation target is sharp (IPD/focus reminder). Occlusion (optional, off by default, product owner 2026-10-18: the headset already blocks outside light well): during the exam the untested eye always receives black and both eyes stay open; this short check before each eye makes the patient close the tested eye for occlusionWindowMs while a bright disc is shown to the tested eye only, and a press means light reaches the untested eye (stop, call the doctor).

_ageDoc: Used only when no exam order file provides the age; the operator adjusts it on the setup screen. Age drives the ZEST prior and the normative comparison.

presentation._doc: Rendering details outside the psychophysics. fallbackIpdMm is used only when the runtime gives no eye positions (desktop preview); it is logged. Text is dark grey on the background, below the fixation target.

sync._doc: Phase 4: optional link to the doctor portal (docs/SYNC_API.md). The exam never depends on it: files are written locally first and sent later; without portal.json / portal-token.json on the headset the flow is the Phase 2 one. liveIntervalMs is the maximum gap between live snapshots; retryBackoffMs is applied in order after consecutive network failures, then the last value repeats.
